- If sentiment is consistently high (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak by 2–5%.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3), model underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >3%), model often overcorrects; reduce next period’s forecast by 1–3%.
- Model frequently overshoots in early periods of a 30-day forecast; apply a 1–2% downward bias to first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in that window.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate near-term (first 10 days); apply 1–3% downward correction for days 1–10.
- If sentiment is high but price moves lower than forecast, model may be “sentiment-driven”; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3 days.
